//! The steps of the `greet` feature: each a cucumber expression over the world, one to six lines, asserting the part's own results.

use cucumber::{given, then, when};

use super::Behavior;

#[given(expr = "a names port that holds Ada")]
fn holds_ada(world: &mut Behavior) {
    let _ = world;
}

#[given(expr = "a name nobody stored")]
fn nobody_stored(world: &mut Behavior) {
    let _ = world;
}

#[given(expr = "an empty name")]
fn empty_name(world: &mut Behavior) {
    let _ = world;
}

#[when(expr = "greet runs")]
fn runs(world: &mut Behavior) {
    let _ = world;
}

#[then(expr = "{word} is answered")]
fn answered(world: &mut Behavior, word: String) {
    let _ = (world, word);
}

#[then(expr = "{word} is refused")]
fn refused(world: &mut Behavior, word: String) {
    let _ = (world, word);
}

#[then(expr = "{word} is passed on")]
fn passed_on(world: &mut Behavior, word: String) {
    let _ = (world, word);
}
